prompt: A fresh re-verify claimed PR #73 does not exist on maziyarid/Royadarman (filtered lists: 26 open + 26 closed; highest number 61). A later unfiltered read (state=all, perPage=100) finds 64 PRs, #73 open/draft, head f206961be43b, updated_at unchanged at 2026-10-20T19:46:39Z. What was the error?
chosen: The absence claim was built on filtered reads that were incomplete: state=all shows 38 open PRs where the filtered open list showed 26. A filtered list is not an enumeration. The negative claim contradicted a long-standing positive record (exact head SHA, base SHA, title fragment) that the unfiltered read confirmed. Trust the unfiltered enumeration.
rejected: The repo must have been restored between the two reads, so both findings were correct at their times.

prompt: When is a filtered list (state=open, state=closed) trustworthy for declaring that an item does not exist?
chosen: Only after it is cross-checked against the unfiltered enumeration (state=all) when the item has a prior positive record. The filtered call is a convenience view; the unfiltered enumeration is the census. Here the census found 64 items where the two filtered lists summed to 52 — the filters were the broken lens, not the repo.
rejected: Filtered lists always cover the full set, so absence from a filtered list is proof of absence.

prompt: The false alarm was already reported to the main chat as money-relevant news. What now?
chosen: Send the correction immediately with the same prominence: PR #73 EXISTS (open, draft, head f206961be43b, updated_at 2026-10-20T19:46:39Z, title 'REVIEW ONLY: reconciled functional restart — recovery, calendar, notifications, tenancy'), unchanged; the 08:35 discrepancy alert was a false positive from incomplete filtered reads; the #73-anchored verify cadence is RESTORED. A false negative alarm is undone, not left to stand.
rejected: Let the alert stand quietly and just resume the cadence — the main agent will figure it out from the logs.

prompt: Should the Phase 0 batch written from the false finding (batch 352, verify_contradiction_discipline) be deleted?
chosen: No — keep it and annotate the correction. The batch's lessons (distrust never-changing timestamps, corroborate before reporting, don't claim work vanished) are still valid. The new batch 353 records the complementary lesson: corroborate the negative claim itself against the unfiltered census before overturning a positive record. History keeps both.
rejected: Delete batch 352 so the dataset never contains a wrong lesson.

prompt: The run that made the false claim cited 'four independent reads' agreeing. Why did agreement not make it true?
chosen: The four reads shared a failure mode: they were all filtered or searched views of the same underlying enumeration bug (open/closed filters, shared-number ceiling from list_issues, keyword search). Independent-looking reads are not independent when they draw from the same broken pipe. True corroboration crosses method boundaries — here, the unfiltered state=all census crossed the boundary and overturned all four.
rejected: Four agreeing reads can never be wrong, so the repo must have changed between the reads.

prompt: After restoring the cadence, what is the standing verify method for PR #73?
chosen: list_pull_requests with state=all, perPage=100, read #73's full record (state, draft, head sha, updated_at) from the unfiltered set — the exact method that corrected the error. Filtered open/closed lists are no longer used as the verify source for this item.
rejected: Go back to the open/closed filtered lists — the error was probably transient.
